Label: Abrasive Finishing
Definition: A finishing process that uses abrasive particles or tools to remove small amounts of material and improve surface texture or appearance.

Label: Additive Manufacturing
Definition: A process that builds objects layer by layer from digital models by depositing or solidifying material, enabling complex geometries and rapid prototyping.

Label: Directed Energy Deposition
Definition: A process that uses focused thermal energy (laser, electron beam, or plasma arc) to melt and deposit material simultaneously for near-net-shape parts or repairs.

Label: Drop On Demand
Also Called: DoD Printing, Inkjet 3D Printing, Drop-Based 3D Printing, Binder Droplet Printing
Definition: An additive manufacturing process that deposits liquid material in controlled droplets to build parts layer by layer.

Label: Fused Deposition Modeling
Also Called: FDM, Fused Filament Fabrication, FFF, Filament 3D Printing, Plastic 3D Printing, Melted Filament Printing, Extrusion 3D Printing
Definition: An additive manufacturing process where a thermoplastic filament is melted and extruded through a nozzle to form layers of a part.

Label: Fused Filament Fabrication
Also Called: FFF, Filament 3D Printing, Plastic 3D Printing, FDM, Extrusion Printing
Hierarchy: Additive Manufacturing > Fused Deposition Modeling > Fused Filament Fabrication
Definition: A material extrusion process that builds parts by depositing molten thermoplastic filament in successive layers.

Label: Laminated Object Manufacturing
Also Called: LOM, Sheet Lamination, Layered Sheet Printing, Paper 3D Printing
Definition: An additive process where thin sheets of material are bonded and cut layer by layer to form a 3D object.

Label: Metal Additive Manufacturing
Also Called: Metal 3D Printing, Metal AM, Metal-Based Additive Manufacturing, Direct Metal Printing
Definition: Additive manufacturing techniques that create metal parts by selectively melting, fusing, or depositing metal material.

Label: Polymer Deposition
Also Called: Polymer Extrusion, Polymer 3D Printing, Plastic Deposition Printing, Thermoplastic Printing
Definition: An additive process that extrudes or deposits thermoplastic materials layer by layer to form components.

Label: Powder Deposition
Also Called: Powder-Based Additive Manufacturing, Powder Deposition Printing, Blown Powder 3D Printing
Definition: An additive process where powdered material is delivered to a heat source and fused to build 3D parts.

Label: Selective Laser Melting
Hierarchy: Additive Manufacturing > Powder Bed Fusion > Selective Laser Melting
Definition: A laser-based PBF process that fully melts metal powders to create near-wrought-quality dense parts.

Label: Powder Bed Fusion
Definition: A process where a heat source (laser or electron beam) selectively fuses regions of a powder bed layer by layer to build parts.

Label: Selective Laser Sintering
Hierarchy: Additive Manufacturing > Powder Bed Fusion > Selective Laser Sintering
Definition: A PBF process that sinters polymer or composite powders using a laser, producing functional and durable parts.

Label: Selective Mask Sintering
Also Called: SMS, Mask-Based Sintering, Mask Sintering 3D Printing
Definition: A powder-bed process where a mask defines areas of heating to selectively sinter powdered material into solid layers.

Label: Solid Deposition
Also Called: Solid Freeform Fabrication, SFF, Solid Deposition Modeling, SDM
Definition: An additive manufacturing method that deposits solid material in precise patterns to build 3D structures.

Label: Stereolithography
Definition: A vat photopolymerization process that uses a UV laser to cure liquid resin layer by layer into solid parts.

Label: Photopolymerization
Also Called: Vat Photopolymerization, Resin Curing, UV Resin Printing, Digital Light Processing, DLP
Definition: A process that cures liquid photopolymer resin into solid layers using a light source such as UV or lasers.

Label: Binder Jetting
Definition: A 3D printing process where a liquid binding agent is selectively deposited onto a powder bed to bond particles together and form solid parts.

Label: Casting
Definition: A manufacturing process where liquid material (metal, plastic, or ceramic) is poured into a mold and solidified into the desired shape.

Label: Carbon Dioxide Mold Casting
Definition: A sand casting process where sodium silicate sand molds are hardened by passing carbon dioxide gas through the mold.

Label: Centrifugal Casting
Definition: A casting method where molten metal is poured into a rapidly rotating mold, using centrifugal force to distribute the metal and reduce impurities.

Label: Ceramic Mold Casting
Definition: A precision casting process that uses a ceramic mold made from a fired slurry, producing smooth, heat-resistant molds for complex shapes.

Label: Continuous Casting
Definition: A process where molten metal is solidified into a continuous billet, slab, or bloom for further rolling or forming.

Label: Die Casting
Definition: A high-pressure casting process where molten metal is forced into a hardened steel mold cavity, enabling mass production of detailed parts.

Label: Cold Chamber Die Casting
Hierarchy: Casting > Die Casting > Cold Chamber Die Casting
Definition: A die casting process where molten metal is ladled into a cold chamber before being forced into the die under high pressure.

Label: Hot Chamber Die Casting
Hierarchy: Casting > Die Casting > Hot Chamber Die Casting
Definition: A die casting process where the injection system is immersed in molten metal, allowing faster cycle times for low-melting alloys.

Label: Gravity Casting
Definition: A casting process where molten metal is poured into a mold under the force of gravity, without additional pressure.

Label: Permanent Mold Casting
Hierarchy: Casting > Die Casting > Permanent Mold Casting
Definition: A process where molten metal is poured by gravity into reusable metal molds, producing consistent and durable castings.

Label: Investment Casting
Definition: A precision casting method where a wax pattern is coated in ceramic, then melted away to leave a mold cavity for metal pouring.

Label: Lost Foam Casting
Definition: A casting process where a foam pattern is embedded in sand and vaporized by molten metal, leaving a cavity that forms the final part.

Label: Plaster Mold Casting
Definition: A casting process using gypsum-based plaster molds to achieve fine detail and smooth surface finishes.

Label: Sand Casting
Definition: A versatile casting process that uses sand molds to shape molten metal, suitable for large, simple, or custom parts.

Label: Shell Molding
Definition: A casting method where a thin shell of sand and resin is hardened around a pattern to form the mold.

Label: Spin Casting
Definition: A centrifugal casting method where molds are spun to distribute molten material evenly, often used for small or jewelry parts.

Label: Squeeze Casting
Definition: A hybrid of casting and forging where molten metal is poured into a mold and then compressed to eliminate porosity.

Label: Vacuum Casting
Definition: A casting process where molten metal or resin is drawn into the mold cavity by vacuum pressure, improving detail and reducing porosity.

Label: Chemical Processing
Definition: A manufacturing category involving the use of chemical reactions or treatments to modify or produce materials.

Label: Electrochemical Processes
Definition: Processes that use controlled electric current in an electrolyte to remove, deposit, or modify material surfaces.

Label: Fabricating
Definition: The process of constructing products by cutting, shaping, and assembling raw materials, usually metal or plastic.

Label: Kitting
Definition: An assembly preparation process where individual parts are grouped together into kits for efficient manufacturing or packaging.

Label: Micro Fabrication
Definition: Manufacturing processes used to create extremely small structures, typically on the micrometer or nanometer scale.

Label: Semiconductor Fabricating
Definition: The process of manufacturing semiconductor devices using photolithography, deposition, etching, and doping techniques.

Label: Wire Harness Assembly
Definition: The process of assembling cables and connectors into organized harnesses for electrical systems.

Label: Filament Winding
Definition: A composite manufacturing process where continuous fibers are wound over a rotating mandrel and impregnated with resin.

Label: Forging
Definition: A process that shapes metal using compressive forces, typically with hammers or presses, to improve strength and grain structure.

Label: Coining
Definition: A precision forging process where material is compressed in closed dies to form fine details and surface features.

Label: Cold Forging
Definition: A forging process performed at room temperature, producing precise parts with improved strength and surface finish.

Label: Die Forging
Definition: A forging process where heated metal is shaped between two dies that contain a shaped cavity.

Label: Drop Forging
Definition: A forging method where a hammer or press drops onto heated metal to shape it inside a die cavity.

Label: Impression Die Forging
Definition: A forging method where metal is pressed into a closed die cavity, taking the shape of the die for complex geometries.

Label: Open Die Forging
Definition: A forging method where metal is deformed between flat or simple dies, used for large, simple shapes.

Label: Heading
Definition: A forging process that forms heads on fasteners such as bolts, screws, and rivets by upsetting the metal.

Label: Press Forging
Definition: A forging process using a mechanical or hydraulic press to gradually apply pressure and shape the metal.

Label: Roll Forging
Definition: A forging technique where metal is passed through rotating rolls with shaped grooves to reduce thickness and form profiles.

Label: Swedging
Definition: A forging process that reduces the diameter or changes the shape of a workpiece by repeated hammering or pressing.

Label: Upset Forging
Definition: A forging method that increases the cross-section of a material by compressing its length,commonly used for fasteners and bolts.

Label: Upsetting
Definition: A forging technique where the length of a metal piece is reduced while its cross-sectional area increases, often for fasteners.

Label: Forming
Definition: A category of manufacturing processes that shape materials into desired forms without adding or removing material.

Label: Cold Forming
Definition: A forming process performed at or near room temperature to plastically deform material into shape.

Label: Sheet Forming
Definition: A set of processes used to shape sheet metal into parts through bending, stretching, or stamping.

Label: Drawing
Definition: A forming process where metal is pulled through a die to reduce diameter or alter cross-section, often used for wires and tubes.

Label: Bar Drawing
Definition: A process of reducing the diameter of bars by pulling them through a die for size control and surface finish.

Label: Ironing
Definition: A sheet metal forming process that reduces wall thickness while maintaining or increasing height, commonly used in cans.

Label: Cold Drawing
Definition: A drawing operation performed at room temperature, improving dimensional accuracy and surface finish.

Label: Deep Drawing
Definition: A forming process where sheet metal is stretched into a die to create deep, hollow shapes such as cups or cans.

Label: Tube Drawing
Definition: A method of reducing the diameter and wall thickness of tubes by pulling them through a die.

Label: Wire Drawing
Definition: A process where wire is drawn through a series of dies to decrease its diameter and increase tensile strength.

Label: Electro Forming
Definition: A process where metal is deposited onto a mold or mandrel using electroplating to build up precise parts.

Label: Explosion Forming
Definition: A high-energy forming process where an explosive charge creates pressure waves to shape metal against a die.

Label: Extruding
Also Called: Extrusion, Metal Extrusion, Plastic Extrusion, Profile Extrusion
Definition: A forming process where material is forced through a die to create continuous objects with a fixed cross-section.

Label: Cold Extrusion
Definition: An extrusion process performed at room temperature, yielding precise dimensions and improved mechanical properties.

Label: Direct Extrusion
Definition: An extrusion method where the billet and ram move in the same direction to push material through a die.

Label: Hot Extrusion
Definition: An extrusion process performed at elevated temperatures to reduce material resistance and form complex cross-sections.

Label: Indirect Extrusion
Definition: An extrusion process where the die moves into the billet, causing metal to flow in the opposite direction of the ram.

Label: Flow Forming
Definition: A cold forming process that elongates and thins a cylindrical blank over a rotating mandrel using rollers.

Label: Hot Forming
Definition: A forming process performed at elevated temperatures to improve ductility and reduce forming forces.

Label: Hydroforming
Definition: A process where pressurized fluid forms ductile metals into lightweight, complex shapes, often used in automotive parts.

Label: Knurling
Definition: A machining and forming process that creates patterned ridges on a workpiece surface for grip or decoration.

Label: Metal Forming
Definition: A broad category of processes that plastically deform metal into desired shapes without removing material.

Label: Peen Forming
Definition: A process where repeated mechanical impacts stretch and bend sheet metal into complex curves, often for aerospace parts.

Label: Powder Metal Forming
Definition: A forming process that compacts and shapes powdered metals before sintering into solid parts.

Label: Isostatic Pressing
Hierarchy: Forming > Powder Metal Forming > Isostatic Pressing
Definition: A compaction process that applies equal pressure from all directions to consolidate powders into a dense shape.

Label: Cold Isostatics Pressing
Hierarchy: Forming > Powder Metal Forming > Cold Isostatics Pressing
Definition: A variant of isostatic pressing performed at room temperature, using fluid pressure to compact powders.

Label: Powder Compacting
Hierarchy: Forming > Powder Metal Forming > Powder Compacting
Definition: The process of pressing metal or ceramic powders in a die to form a solid green compact.

Label: Powder Metallurgy
Definition: A process of manufacturing components from powdered metals through compaction and sintering.

Label: Spark Plasma Sintering
Hierarchy: Forming > Powder Metallurgy > Spark Plasma Sintering
Definition: A sintering technique that uses pulsed electric current and pressure to rapidly densify powdered materials.

Label: Press Forming
Definition: A surface finishing method where materials or coatings are shaped or bonded to a substrate using mechanical pressing.

Label: Roll Die Engraving
Definition: A process where patterns or designs are engraved onto a workpiece surface using engraved rolling dies.

Label: Roll Forming
Definition: A continuous bending process where sheet metal passes through a series of rollers to produce long profiles.

Label: Roller Forming
Definition: A forming process where rollers progressively shape sheet or strip material into a desired cross-section.

Label: Rolling
Definition: A metal forming process that reduces thickness or changes cross-section by compressing material between rotating rolls.

Label: Cold Rolling
Also Called: Cold Rolled Metal, Cold Reduction Rolling
Definition: A metal forming process where metal is compressed between rollers at room temperature to improve strength and finish.

Label: Flat Rolling
Definition: A rolling process that reduces the thickness of flat sheet or strip material between parallel rolls.

Label: Hot Rolling
Definition: A process where heated metal is passed through rollers to reduce thickness and refine grain structure.

Label: Plate Rolling
Definition: A rolling process where metal plates are passed through rolls to reduce thickness or form curves.

Label: Ring Rolling
Definition: A hot forming process where a thick-walled ring is rolled to a larger diameter with reduced thickness.

Label: Shape Rolling
Definition: A rolling process where rolls with profiled grooves form metal into specific cross-sectional shapes.

Label: Sheet Rolling
Definition: A rolling method to produce thin sheets of uniform thickness from metal slabs.

Label: Sheet Metal Rolling
Definition: A process of passing sheet metal through rolls to reduce thickness or impart curvature.

Label: Thread Rolling
Definition: A cold forming process that produces threads on fasteners by pressing dies into the workpiece surface.

Label: Shear Forming
Definition: A spinning process where localized pressure thins sheet metal while maintaining diameter.

Label: Spin Forming
Definition: A process where a rotating metal blank is gradually deformed over a mandrel using rollers or tools.

Label: Superplastic Forming
Definition: A forming process that exploits the superplasticity of certain alloys at high temperature to form complex shapes.

Label: Swagging
Definition: A forging process where a workpiece is reduced in diameter by hammering or rotary dies.

Label: Thermoforming
Definition: A plastic forming process where heated sheets are shaped over molds by vacuum, pressure, or mechanical force.

Label: Roll Bonding
Definition: A solid-state joining process where two or more layers of material are bonded together by rolling pressure.

Label: Vacuum Thermoforming
Definition: A thermoforming process where a heated plastic sheet is pulled into a mold by vacuum pressure.

Label: Tubing
Definition: A forming category covering processes that manufacture metal or plastic tubes with defined shapes and dimensions.

Label: Custom Tubing
Definition: Specialized tubing manufactured to meet unique size, shape, or material requirements for specific applications.

Label: Cut to Length Tubing
Hierarchy: Forming > Tubing > Cut to Length Tubing
Definition: Tubing that is manufactured and precisely cut into predetermined lengths for downstream assembly or processing.

Label: Fractional Tubing
Definition: Standardized tubing sized in fractional inch dimensions, often used in laboratory and fluid systems.

Label: Hypodermic Tubing
Definition: Very small-diameter tubing with tight tolerances, commonly used for medical needles and fluid delivery systems.

Label: Metric Tubing
Definition: Tubing sized according to metric dimensions, widely used in international fluid, gas, and structural systems.

Label: Square Tubing
Definition: Hollow tubing with square or rectangular cross-sections, commonly used in frames, supports, and structures.

Label: Vacuum Forming
Definition: A plastic forming process where a heated sheet is drawn against a mold using vacuum pressure.

Label: Vacuum Pressing
Definition: A forming technique where vacuum pressure compresses materials, often used for composites or powder compaction.

Label: Cold Vacuum Pressing
Hierarchy: Forming > Vacuum Pressing > Cold Vacuum Pressing
Definition: A vacuum pressing method performed at room temperature to compact powders without heating.

Label: Hot Vacuum Pressing
Hierarchy: Forming > Vacuum Pressing > Hot Vacuum Pressing
Definition: A process combining heat and vacuum pressure to densify powders or composites into solid parts.

Label: Hot Isostatic
Definition: A process that applies high temperature and isostatic gas pressure to densify metals, ceramics, or composites.

Label: Wire Forming
Definition: A process of shaping wire into specific forms or components using bending, coiling, or stamping tools.

Label: Heat Treating
Definition: A group of processes that heat and cool metals under controlled conditions to alter mechanical or physical properties.

Label: Annealing
Definition: A heat treatment that softens material, improves ductility, and relieves internal stresses through controlled heating and cooling.

Label: Recovery Annealing
Definition: A process that reduces internal stresses and restores some ductility without significant changes to grain structure.

Label: Stress Relieving
Definition: A heat treatment applied to reduce residual stresses from machining, welding, or forming without altering hardness.

Label: Tempering
Definition: A heat treatment applied after hardening to reduce brittleness and increase toughness of metals.

Label: Recrystallization
Definition: A process where deformed grains in cold-worked metals are replaced by new, strain-free grains upon heating.

Label: Full Annealing
Definition: A heat treatment involving heating above critical temperature and slow cooling to produce soft, ductile material.

Label: Process Annealing
Definition: A subcritical annealing process used to soften cold-worked metals and restore ductility for further forming.

Label: Cold Working
Definition: The process of deforming metal below its recrystallization temperature to increase strength through strain hardening.

Label: Hot Working
Definition: The process of shaping metals at temperatures above recrystallization, improving ductility and reducing strength.

Label: Short Cycle Annealing
Definition: A faster annealing method with reduced heating and cooling times, applied for stress relief and ductility restoration.

Label: Cold Treatment
Definition: A process that exposes metals to sub-zero temperatures to transform retained austenite and improve hardness.

Label: Hardening
Definition: A heat treatment that increases hardness and strength of metals by heating and then rapid cooling (quenching).

Label: Quench Hardening
Definition: A process where steel is heated to austenitizing temperature and rapidly cooled to form martensite, increasing hardness.

Label: Quenching
Definition: Rapid cooling of heated metals in water, oil, or gas to alter structure and improve hardness or strength.

Label: Surface Hardening
Definition: A heat treatment that hardens only the surface of a component while retaining a tough, ductile core.

Label: Chromizing
Hierarchy: Heat Treating > Hardening > Surface Hardening > Chromizing
Definition: A diffusion process where chromium is introduced into the surface of steel to improve hardness and corrosion resistance.

Label: Cyaniding
Hierarchy: Heat Treating > Hardening > Surface Hardening > Cyaniding
Definition: A case hardening process where steel is heated in a cyanide bath to add carbon and nitrogen for surface hardening.

Label: Diffusion Hardening
Hierarchy: Heat Treating > Hardening > Surface Hardening > Diffusion Hardening
Definition: A group of processes where alloying elements diffuse into the surface of metals to increase hardness and wear resistance.

Label: Carbonitriding
Hierarchy: Heat Treating > Hardening > Surface Hardening > Carbonitriding
Definition: A thermochemical process where carbon and nitrogen diffuse into steel surface, improving hardness and fatigue resistance.

Label: Carburizing
Hierarchy: Heat Treating > Hardening > Surface Hardening > Carburizing
Definition: A case hardening method where steel is exposed to a carbon-rich atmosphere at high temperature to harden the surface.

Label: Nitriding
Hierarchy: Heat Treating > Hardening > Surface Hardening > Nitriding
Definition: A process that diffuses nitrogen into steel surface at sub-critical temperatures, forming hard nitrides for wear resistance.

Label: Flame Hardening
Hierarchy: Heat Treating > Hardening > Surface Hardening > Flame Hardening
Definition: A method of heating the surface of steel with a high-temperature flame followed by rapid quenching for surface hardening.

Label: Oxyacetylene Cutting
Definition: A thermal cutting process using oxygen and acetylene flame to cut through metals by oxidizing and melting.

Label: Induction Hardening
Hierarchy: Heat Treating > Hardening > Surface Hardening > Induction Hardening
Definition: A surface hardening method where induction heating raises temperature rapidly, followed by quenching.

Label: Vacuum Hardening
Hierarchy: Heat Treating > Hardening > Surface Hardening > Vacuum Hardening
Definition: A hardening process performed in vacuum furnaces to minimize oxidation and decarburization during heat treatment.

Label: Through Hardening
Definition: A heat treatment where the entire cross-section of a component is hardened, not just the surface.

Label: Age Quench Hardening
Hierarchy: Heat Treating > Hardening > Age Quench Hardening
Definition: A process combining solution heat treatment, quenching, and aging to improve strength and hardness in alloys.

Label: Air Quench Hardening
Hierarchy: Heat Treating > Hardening > Air Quench Hardening
Definition: A quenching method where air is used as the cooling medium for moderate hardening.

Label: Austempering
Definition: A heat treatment where steel is quenched and held in a bainitic temperature range, improving toughness and ductility.

Label: Martempering
Definition: A process where steel is quenched into a bath just above martensite start temperature, equalized, then cooled to reduce stresses.

Label: Oil Quench Hardening
Hierarchy: Heat Treating > Hardening > Oil Quench Hardening
Definition: A hardening method where oil is used as the quenching medium to balance hardness and minimize distortion.

Label: Water Quench Hardening
Hierarchy: Heat Treating > Hardening > Water Quench Hardening
Definition: A hardening method where water is used as the quenching medium for rapid cooling and maximum hardness.

Label: Sintering
Definition: A process of compacting and forming solid materials by applying heat below melting point to bond particles.

Label: Induction Heading
Definition: A forming process where induction heating softens the end of a metal bar or wire, enabling it to be upset or headed into shape.

Label: Joining
Definition: A group of processes that permanently or temporarily connect two or more materials or components.

Label: Adhesive Bonding
Definition: A joining method using adhesives to bond materials at their surfaces without melting or deforming them.

Label: Lamination
Definition: A process of joining layers of material together, usually with adhesives, heat, or pressure, to form a composite.

Label: Fusion Joining
Definition: A process where materials are joined by melting their faying surfaces, often with filler, to form a solid joint.

Label: Heat Sealing
Definition: A process that uses heat and pressure to bond thermoplastic materials together at their interface.

Label: Mechanical Joining
Definition: A joining method using physical fasteners or deformation techniques such as screws, rivets, or bolts.

Label: Mechanical Welding
Definition: A solid-state joining process that uses mechanical energy, such as pressure and friction, rather than melting.

Label: Explosive Welding
Definition: A solid-state welding process where controlled explosive energy drives metals together at high velocity to bond.

Label: Friction Welding
Definition: A welding process where heat generated from friction between surfaces, combined with pressure, creates a solid-state bond.

Label: Friction Stri Welding
Hierarchy: Joining > Mechanical Joining > Mechanical Welding > Friction Welding > Friction Stri Welding
Definition: A solid-state welding technique where a rotating tool stirs and fuses material along the joint line without melting.

Label: Pressure Welding
Definition: A solid-state joining process where external pressure alone bonds materials without significant heat input.

Label: Ultrasonic Welding
Definition: A process where high-frequency vibrations under pressure cause solid-state bonding of materials, especially plastics and thin metals.

Label: Press Fitting
Definition: A joining technique where a slightly oversized part is forced into another, creating an interference fit.

Label: Shrink Fitting
Definition: A method where one component is heated or cooled to allow insertion into another, forming a tight fit upon temperature equalization.

Label: Riveting
Definition: A permanent joining method where a rivet is deformed to clamp materials together.

Label: Metal Joining
Definition: A broad category of processes specifically for bonding metal parts by welding, brazing, soldering, or fastening.

Label: Thermal Joining
Definition: A group of processes that use heat energy (e.g., welding, brazing, soldering) to bond materials.

Label: Brazing
Definition: A process where a filler metal with a lower melting point flows into the joint between base metals without melting them.

Label: Dip Brazing
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Brazing > Dip Brazing
Definition: A brazing method where assemblies are immersed in a molten salt or metal bath to heat and join components.

Label: Clinching
Definition: A mechanical joining process where sheets are deformed locally to interlock without additional fasteners or heat.

Label: Furnace Brazing
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Brazing > Furnace Brazing
Definition: A brazing process carried out in a controlled-atmosphere furnace for precise heating and uniform joints.

Label: Induction Brazing
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Brazing > Induction Brazing
Definition: A brazing process that uses induction heating to rapidly heat the joint area and melt filler metal.

Label: Infrared Brazing
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Brazing > Infrared Brazing
Definition: A brazing method using infrared radiation as the heat source to melt filler material and form joints.

Label: Laser Brazing
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Brazing > Laser Brazing
Definition: A precise brazing process using a focused laser beam as the heat source for localized bonding.

Label: Resistance Brazing
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Brazing > Resistance Brazing
Definition: A brazing process where electrical resistance heating is used to melt filler metal at the joint.

Label: Torch Brazing
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Brazing > Torch Brazing
Definition: A manual brazing process where a gas-fueled torch heats the joint and melts filler metal.

Label: Vacuum Brazing
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Brazing > Vacuum Brazing
Definition: A brazing process performed in a vacuum furnace, providing clean joints free of oxidation and flux.

Label: Soldering
Definition: A low-temperature joining process where a filler metal (solder) melts below 450 °C to bond components without melting the base metals.

Label: Dip Soldering
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Soldering > Dip Soldering
Definition: A soldering method where components are dipped into a molten solder bath to create joints.

Label: Induction Soldering
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Soldering > Induction Soldering
Definition: A soldering process using induction heating to melt solder at the joint area quickly and precisely.

Label: Infrared Soldering
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Soldering > Infrared Soldering
Definition: A soldering method that employs infrared radiation to heat and melt solder, often used in electronics assembly.

Label: Iron Soldering
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Soldering > Iron Soldering
Definition: A manual soldering process using a heated soldering iron tip to melt and apply solder to joints.

Label: Resistance Soldering
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Soldering > Resistance Soldering
Definition: A soldering process where electrical resistance generates localized heat to melt solder at the joint.

Label: Torch Soldering
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Soldering > Torch Soldering
Definition: A soldering method that uses a flame torch to heat the workpiece and melt solder.

Label: Ultrasonic Soldering
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Soldering > Ultrasonic Soldering
Definition: A fluxless soldering process that uses ultrasonic vibrations to disrupt oxides and allow wetting of the solder.

Label: Wave Soldering
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Soldering > Wave Soldering
Definition: An automated soldering process where assembled circuit boards pass over a wave of molten solder for mass joining.

Label: Thermal Welding
Definition: A joining process that uses heat to melt and fuse materials together into a solid bond.

Label: Braze Welding
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Thermal Welding > Braze Welding
Definition: A process where filler metal is deposited with a welding torch to join parts without fully melting the base metal.

Label: Carbon Arc Brazing
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Thermal Welding > Braze Welding > Carbon Arc Brazing
Definition: A brazing process that uses a carbon electrode arc to heat filler metal for joining parts.

Label: Gas Brazing
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Thermal Welding > Braze Welding > Gas Brazing
Definition: A brazing method that uses a gas flame torch to heat filler metal and join components.

Label: Diffusion Bonding
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Thermal Welding > Diffusion Bonding
Definition: A solid-state joining process where materials bond through atomic diffusion under heat and pressure without melting.

Label: Electric Arc Welding
Also Called: Arc Welding, Manual Metal Arc Welding, MMAW
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Thermal Welding > Electric Arc Welding
Definition: A welding process that uses an electric arc between an electrode and the workpiece to melt and join metals.

Label: Carbon Arc Welding
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Thermal Welding > Electric Arc Welding > Carbon Arc Welding
Definition: An arc welding method that employs a carbon electrode to create heat for fusing base materials.

Label: Flux-Cored Arc Welding
Also Called: FCAW, Flux Core Welding, Self-Shielded Welding
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Thermal Welding > Electric Arc Welding > Flux-Cored Arc Welding
Definition: A welding process that uses a continuously fed tubular wire filled with flux, providing shielding and filler material.

Label: Gas Metal Arc Welding
Also Called: GMAW, MIG Welding, Metal Inert Gas Welding
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Thermal Welding > Electric Arc Welding > Gas Metal Arc Welding
Definition: An arc welding process that melts and joins metals using a consumable wire electrode and an external shielding gas.

Label: MIG Welding
Also Called: Gas Metal Arc Welding, GMAW, Metal Inert Gas Welding
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Thermal Welding > Electric Arc Welding > Gas Metal Arc Welding > MIG Welding
Definition: A welding process where a consumable wire electrode is fed through a welding gun and melted by an electric arc, shielded by inert gas.

Label: Pulsed Gas Metal Arc Welding
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Thermal Welding > Electric Arc Welding > Gas Metal Arc Welding > Pulsed Gas Metal Arc Welding
Definition: A variation of GMAW that alternates current between high and low levels, improving control, reducing spatter, and allowing welding of thin materials.

Label: Gas Tungsten Arc Welding
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Thermal Welding > Electric Arc Welding > Gas Tungsten Arc Welding
Definition: A precise arc welding process where a non-consumable tungsten electrode creates the arc and shielding gas protects the weld pool.

Label: Pulsed Gas Tungsten Arc Welding
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Thermal Welding > Electric Arc Welding > Gas Tungsten Arc Welding > Pulsed Gas Tungsten Arc Welding
Definition: A variant of GTAW where current pulses between high and low levels to improve heat control and weld quality.

Label: TIG Welding

Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Thermal Welding > Electric Arc Welding > Gas Tungsten Arc Welding > TIG Welding
Definition: A common name for Gas Tungsten Arc Welding, where a tungsten electrode and inert gas are used to produce high-quality welds.

Label: Shielded Metal Arc Welding
Also Called: Stick Welding, SMAW, Manual Metal Arc Welding
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Thermal Welding > Electric Arc Welding > Shielded Metal Arc Welding
Definition: A manual welding process using a flux-coated consumable electrode that melts to form the weld joint and protective slag.

Label: Stud Welding

Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Thermal Welding > Electric Arc Welding > Stud Welding
Definition: A welding process where a metal fastener (stud) is joined to a base metal using an arc, commonly for construction and automotive applications.

Label: Submerged Arc Welding
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Thermal Welding > Electric Arc Welding > Submerged Arc Welding
Definition: A welding process where the arc is submerged beneath a blanket of granular flux, which shields and stabilizes the weld.

Label: Electrical Resistance Welding
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Thermal Welding > Electrical Resistance Welding

Label: Butt Welding
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Thermal Welding > Electrical Resistance Welding > Butt Welding
Definition: A type of resistance welding where two parts are joined end-to-end by applying pressure and passing current through the contact.

Label: Electro Slag Welding
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Thermal Welding > Electrical Resistance Welding > Electro Slag Welding
Definition: A high-deposition welding process where molten slag conducts electricity and generates heat to fuse thick sections vertically.

Label: Percussion Welding
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Thermal Welding > Electrical Resistance Welding > Percussion Welding
Definition: A resistance welding process using a sudden discharge of electrical energy and pressure to instantly join metals.

Label: Projection Welding
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Thermal Welding > Electrical Resistance Welding > Projection Welding
Definition: A resistance welding process where raised projections on one part localize heat and pressure, commonly for fasteners.

Label: Resistance Welding
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Thermal Welding > Electrical Resistance Welding > Resistance Welding
Definition: A family of welding processes using heat from electrical resistance and force to form joints, including spot and seam welding.

Label: Seam Welding
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Thermal Welding > Electrical Resistance Welding > Seam Welding
Definition: A resistance welding process where electrodes roll along a joint, producing a continuous or intermittent weld seam.

Label: Metal Clinching
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Thermal Welding > Electrical Resistance Welding > Seam Welding > Metal Clinching
Definition: A mechanical joining process that locks sheet metals together by deforming them without heat, sometimes grouped under resistance joining.

Label: Spot Welding
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Thermal Welding > Electrical Resistance Welding > Spot Welding
Definition: A resistance welding process where heat and pressure are applied at small contact points between sheets to create localized welds.

Label: Resistance Spot Welding
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Thermal Welding > Electrical Resistance Welding > Spot Welding > Resistance Spot Welding
Definition: A common spot welding method using copper electrodes to apply current and pressure, widely used in automotive manufacturing.

Label: Fusion Welding
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Thermal Welding > Fusion Welding
Definition: A group of welding processes where heat melts base metals to form a joint, with or without filler material.

Label: Gas Welding
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Thermal Welding > Gas Welding
Definition: A welding process that uses a flame from burning fuel gas with oxygen to melt and join metals.

Label: Atomic Hydrogen Welding
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Thermal Welding > Gas Welding > Atomic Hydrogen Welding
Definition: An arc welding process where hydrogen gas shields and dissociates at the arc, releasing heat to melt the metal.

Label: Combustible Gas Welding
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Thermal Welding > Gas Welding > Combustible Gas Welding
Definition: A category of gas welding processes using fuel gases (such as acetylene or propane) combined with oxygen or air to generate heat.

Label: High Energy Beam Welding
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Thermal Welding > High Energy Beam Welding
Definition: Welding processes that use highly concentrated energy beams, such as electron or laser beams, for deep and precise welds.

Label: Electron Beam Welding
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Thermal Welding > High Energy Beam Welding > Electron Beam Welding
Definition: A fusion welding process where a focused beam of high-velocity electrons generates heat to join metals in a vacuum.

Label: Laser Beam Welding
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Thermal Welding > High Energy Beam Welding > Laser Beam Welding
Definition: A welding process that uses a concentrated laser beam to melt and join metals with high precision and low distortion.

Label: Plasma Arc Welding
Hierarchy: Joining > Thermal Joining > Thermal Welding > High Energy Beam Welding > Plasma Arc Welding
Definition: An arc welding process where a constricted plasma jet produces a high-energy arc for deep and precise weld penetration.

Label: Machining
Definition: A broad manufacturing category where material is selectively removed from a workpiece to achieve desired shape, dimensions, or surface finish.

Label: Abrasive Machining
Definition: A machining process using abrasive particles bonded to wheels, belts, or slurry to remove small amounts of material with high precision.

Label: Buffing
Definition: A finishing process using a soft wheel and fine abrasives to polish a surface to a smooth, reflective finish.

Label: Grinding
Definition: A machining process where a rotating abrasive wheel removes material to achieve tight tolerances and fine surface finishes.

Label: Centerless Grinding
Hierarchy: Machining > Abrasive Machining > Grinding > Centerless Grinding
Definition: A grinding process where the workpiece is supported between a regulating wheel and a grinding wheel without centers.

Label: Creep Feed Grinding

Definition: A grinding technique where the wheel engages the workpiece with a deep cut at slow feed rates for efficient stock removal.

Label: Curvic Grinding

Definition: A specialized grinding process used to produce precise curved gear-tooth profiles or coupling surfaces.

Label: Cylindrical Grinding

Definition: A grinding process used to finish the outside or inside diameter of cylindrical parts to high precision.

Label: CNC Cylindrical Grinding
Hierarchy: Machining > Abrasive Machining > Grinding > Cylindrical Grinding > CNC Cylindrical Grinding
Definition: A computer-controlled cylindrical grinding process for consistent precision and automated production of complex shapes.

Label: Electrochemical Grinding

Definition: A hybrid process combining electrochemical material removal with abrasive action to machine hard or delicate materials.

Label: ECG Tube Cutting
Hierarchy: Machining > Abrasive Machining > Grinding > Electrochemical Grinding > ECG Tube Cutting
Definition: A tube cutting method using electrochemical grinding to produce burr-free and precise cuts on small-diameter tubing.

Label: ID-OD Grinding

Definition: A grinding method for finishing both the internal diameter (ID) and outer diameter (OD) of cylindrical components.

Label: Plunge Grinding
Hierarchy: Machining > Abrasive Machining > Grinding > Plunge Grinding
Definition: A grinding process where the wheel is fed radially into the workpiece without axial movement, suited for grooves and shoulders.

Label: Honing
Definition: A finishing process using abrasive stones to improve dimensional accuracy and surface finish inside holes or cylinders.

Label: Lapping
Definition: A precision finishing process where a workpiece is rubbed against a lap surface with abrasive slurry for extreme accuracy.

Label: CNC Machining
Definition: A subtractive manufacturing process controlled by computer programs, allowing automated and precise cutting of complex parts.

Label: CNC Routing
Definition: A CNC process where a high-speed rotating cutter removes material, often used for wood, plastics, and soft metals.

Label: Five Axis Machining
Hierarchy: Machining > CNC Machining > Five Axis Machining
Definition: Advanced CNC machining with simultaneous movement along five axes, enabling production of complex geometries in one setup.

Label: Seven Axis Machining
Hierarchy: Machining > CNC Machining > Seven Axis Machining
Definition: A highly flexible CNC machining method with movement along seven axes, allowing extremely intricate and precise part production.

Label: Chemical Machining

Label: Chemical Engraving
Definition: A decorative or functional process that uses chemicals to etch patterns, text, or designs into a material’s surface.

Label: Etching
Definition: A process using acids or chemicals to remove selected areas of material, producing detailed patterns or openings.

Label: Chemical Etching

Definition: A controlled etching process using chemical solutions to machine precise features into thin materials.

Label: Photo Etching
Hierarchy: Machining > Chemical Machining > Etching > Photo Etching
Definition: A chemical etching process guided by a photoresist mask to create fine and intricate designs.

Label: Stretching
Definition: A sheet metal forming process where material is pulled and thinned to achieve larger surface dimensions.

Label: Photochemical Machining
Definition: A precise chemical etching process that uses photoresist patterns to produce micro-scale parts from thin sheets.

Label: Deburring
Definition: A finishing process that removes sharp edges or burrs left after machining or cutting operations.

Label: Thermal Deburring
Definition: A process that removes burrs by igniting a combustible gas mixture in a chamber to burn away excess material.

Label: Vibratory Deburring
Definition: A process where parts are tumbled with abrasives in a vibrating container to smooth edges and surfaces.

Label: Electro Chemical Machining
Definition: A machining method where electrical current and an electrolyte dissolve material without mechanical contact.

Label: Engraving
Definition: A process of cutting or carving designs, text, or patterns into a material surface using tools or machines.

Label: Laser Engraving
Definition: A non-contact engraving method where a focused laser beam vaporizes material to mark or etch designs.

Label: Erosion Machining
Definition: A category of machining where material is removed by thermal or electrical energy rather than cutting tools.

Label: Waterjet Cutting

Definition: A cutting process using a high-pressure stream of water, sometimes mixed with abrasives, to cut materials without heat.

Label: Laser Machining
Definition: A subtractive process where lasers cut, drill, or shape materials with high precision and minimal tool wear.

Definition: A variant of broaching where a rotating tool cuts shapes such as hexagons or squares inside holes.

Label: Gear Cutting

Label: Gear Hobbing
Definition: A gear manufacturing process where a rotating hob tool cuts teeth progressively into a gear blank.

Label: Gun Drilling

Definition: A deep hole drilling process that uses a long, straight drill with internal coolant channels for high accuracy.

Label: Trepanning
Hierarchy: Machining > Multipoint Cutting > Hole Making > Drilling > Deep Hole Drilling > Trepanning
Definition: A hole-making process where a circular groove is cut to remove a core of material instead of drilling out all material.

Label: Friction Drilling
Hierarchy: Machining > Multipoint Cutting > Hole Making > Drilling > Friction Drilling
Definition: A drilling process that generates heat through friction to soften material and form a hole without producing chips.

Label: Micro Drilling
Hierarchy: Machining > Multipoint Cutting > Hole Making > Drilling > Micro Drilling
Definition: A precision drilling method used to create extremely small diameter holes, often in electronics or medical devices.

Label: Small Hole Drilling
Hierarchy: Machining > Multipoint Cutting > Hole Making > Drilling > Small Hole Drilling
Definition: A process focused on producing holes of very small diameters using specialized drills and high accuracy.

Label: Perforating

Definition: A process that creates a series of small holes or slits in a material, commonly used in filters, packaging, or sheets.

Label: Reaming
Hierarchy: Machining > Multipoint Cutting > Hole Making > Reaming
Definition: A finishing process that enlarges and smooths an existing drilled hole to precise size and tolerance.

Label: Tapping
Hierarchy: Machining > Multipoint Cutting > Hole Making > Tapping
Definition: A machining process where a tool (tap) cuts internal threads inside a hole for screws or bolts.

Label: Milling
Definition: A versatile machining process where a rotating cutting tool removes material from a workpiece to create shapes and surfaces.

Label: CNC Milling

Definition: Milling performed using computer numerical control, enabling high-precision, automated shaping of complex parts.

Label: Gear Gashing

Definition: A machining operation where material is removed to rough-cut gear teeth before finishing processes.

Label: Horizontal Milling

Definition: A horizontal milling operation where a wide cutter removes large amounts of material in one pass.

Label: End Milling

Label: Face Milling

Definition: A milling process where the cutter’s flat face removes material to create smooth, flat surfaces.

Label: Sawing

Label: Bevelling

Label: Plastic Machining

Label: Diamond Machining

Label: Oil Grooving

Label: Planing
Definition: A machining process where a single-point tool removes material in linear passes to create flat surfaces.

Label: Skiving

Label: Shaping
Definition: A process where a single-point tool moves linearly across a workpiece to cut flat or contoured surfaces.

Label: Turning

Label: Boring

Label: Horizontal Boring
Hierarchy: Machining > Single-Point Cutting > Turning > Boring > Horizontal Boring

Label: Jig Boring
Hierarchy: Machining > Single-Point Cutting > Turning > Boring > Jig Boring
Definition: A high-precision boring process used to achieve extremely accurate hole size and position tolerances.

Definition: A boring process performed with a vertical spindle, often used for large cylindrical parts.

Label: Carbide Machining

Label: Thin Wall Machining

Definition: Precision machining of parts with thin sections while preventing distortion or vibration.

Definition: A precision EDM process that cuts conductive materials using a continuously fed thin wire electrode.

Label: High Energy Beam Machining

Definition: A non-traditional machining method that removes material using concentrated energy beams such as lasers or electrons.

Label: Electron Beam Machining

Definition: A process that uses a focused beam of high-velocity electrons to melt and vaporize material with extreme precision.

Label: Laser Cutting

Definition: A thermal cutting process that uses a focused laser beam to cut, engrave, or shape materials.

Label: CNC Laser Cutting

Definition: Laser cutting controlled by CNC systems to achieve precise, automated cutting of complex geometries.

Label: Laser Etching

Definition: A thermal cutting method where oxygen reacts with preheated metal to oxidize and cut through it.

Label: Plasma Cutting
Hierarchy: Machining > Thermal Subtraction > Torch Cutting > Plasma Cutting
Definition: A process that cuts conductive materials using a high-velocity jet of ionized plasma.

Label: Threading

Label: Ultrasonic Machining
Definition: A non-traditional machining method that uses high-frequency vibrations and abrasive slurry to erode material.

Label: Unconventional Machining
Definition: A group of processes that remove material without traditional cutting tools, often using energy or chemicals.

Label: Zero Stock Machining

Label: Extrusion Blow Molding

Label: Injection Blow Molding

Definition: A process that combines injection molding and blow molding, where a preform is injection molded and then blown into a final hollow shape.

Label: Stretch Blow Molding

Definition: A process in which a plastic preform is both stretched and blown into a mold to improve strength and clarity of bottles.

Label: Compression Molding
Definition: A molding process where material is placed into a heated mold and compressed under pressure to form a part.

Label: Injection Molding
Definition: A high-volume process that injects molten material into a mold cavity, producing complex and precise parts.

Label: Metal Injection Molding
Hierarchy: Molding > Injection Molding > Metal Injection Molding
Definition: A molding process that combines fine metal powders with a binder, injected into molds and then sintered to form solid metal parts.

Label: Reaction Injection Molding
Hierarchy: Molding > Injection Molding > Reaction Injection Molding
Definition: A process where liquid reactants are mixed and injected into a mold, where they chemically react and cure into solid plastic parts.

Label: Rubber Injection Molding
Hierarchy: Molding > Injection Molding > Rubber Injection Molding
Definition: A process that injects heated rubber compounds into a mold to produce durable, elastic components.

Label: Rotational Molding
Definition: A molding process where powdered material is placed in a mold that rotates biaxially while heated, forming hollow parts.

Label: Rotomolding

Label: Resin Transfer Molding

Label: Labeling

Definition: A forming process that bends metal pipes into specific angles or curves without collapsing the cross-section.

Label: Sheet Bending

Definition: A process that bends flat sheet metal into desired angles or profiles using press brakes or rollers.

Label: Tube Bending

Definition: A forming process used to bend hollow tubes into required shapes while maintaining structural integrity.

Label: Wire Bending
Hierarchy: Sheet Metal Processing > Bending > Wire Bending
Definition: A process that bends wire into different configurations for springs, clips, or custom wire forms.

Label: Corrugation

Label: Embossing

Label: Notching

Label: Slitting

Definition: A variation of spinning performed on heated metal to allow forming of thicker or harder materials.

Label: Tufting

Label: Stamping

Definition: Applying a layer of material onto a surface to provide protection, decoration, or functional properties.

Label: Babbitting
Definition: A process of applying a soft metal alloy (babbitt) to bearings for wear resistance and conformability.

Label: Black Oxide Coating
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Coating > Black Oxide Coating
Definition: A chemical conversion process that produces a black oxide layer on metal surfaces for corrosion resistance and appearance.

Label: Chemical Coating
Definition: Surface finishing methods that use chemical reactions to form protective or functional coatings.

Label: Anodizing
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Coating > Chemical Coating > Anodizing
Definition: An electrolytic process that forms a durable oxide layer on aluminum and other metals for corrosion resistance and coloring.

Label: Decorative Anodizing
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Coating > Chemical Coating > Anodizing > Decorative Anodizing
Definition: Anodizing process used to add decorative colors and finishes to metals, especially aluminum.

Label: Iridite
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Coating > Chemical Coating > Iridite
Definition: A chromate-based chemical conversion coating applied to aluminum for corrosion resistance and paint adhesion.

Label: Chemical Conversion Coating
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Coating > Chemical Coating > Chemical Conversion Coating
Definition: A chemical treatment that forms a protective oxide or phosphate layer on metal surfaces.

Label: Alkaline Oxide Conversion Coating
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Coating > Chemical Coating > Chemical Conversion Coating > Alkaline Oxide Conversion Coating
Definition: A conversion coating formed in an alkaline solution to enhance corrosion resistance.

Label: Chromate Conversion Coating
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Coating > Chemical Coating > Chemical Conversion Coating > Chromate Conversion Coating
Definition: A chemical treatment that deposits a protective chromate layer on metals like aluminum and zinc for corrosion protection.

Label: Fused Nitrate Conversion Coating
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Coating > Chemical Coating > Chemical Conversion Coating > Fused Nitrate Conversion Coating
Definition: A conversion coating process using fused nitrates to enhance wear and corrosion resistance.

Label: Phosphate Conversion Coating
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Coating > Chemical Coating > Chemical Conversion Coating > Phosphate Conversion Coating
Definition: A chemical process that creates a phosphate layer on metals for corrosion resistance and paint adhesion.

Label: Phosphating
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Coating > Chemical Coating > Chemical Conversion Coating > Phosphate Conversion Coating > Phosphating
Definition: A surface treatment forming a crystalline phosphate coating to improve corrosion protection and wear resistance.

Label: Plating
Definition: Depositing a metal layer onto a substrate to improve durability, conductivity, or appearance.

Label: Electroplating
Definition: A plating process that uses electric current to deposit a thin metal layer on a conductive surface.

Label: Cadmium Plating
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Coating > Chemical Coating > Plating > Electroplating > Cadmium Plating
Definition: Electroplating with cadmium to provide corrosion resistance and lubricity, often used in aerospace and military applications.

Label: Chrome Plating
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Coating > Chemical Coating > Plating > Electroplating > Chrome Plating
Definition: Electroplating with chromium to enhance hardness, wear resistance, and a bright decorative finish.

Label: Copper Plating
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Coating > Chemical Coating > Plating > Electroplating > Copper Plating
Definition: The electro-deposition of copper onto a substrate, commonly used as an undercoat for improved adhesion and conductivity.

Label: Electro Deposition
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Coating > Chemical Coating > Plating > Electroplating > Copper Plating > Electro Deposition
Definition: A general term for depositing material onto a surface using an electric current, forming a uniform coating.

Label: Electroless Nickel Plating
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Coating > Chemical Coating > Plating > Electroplating > Electroless Nickel Plating
Definition: A chemical (non-electric) plating process that deposits nickel evenly on complex surfaces, providing corrosion and wear resistance.

Label: Gold Plating
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Coating > Chemical Coating > Plating > Electroplating > Gold Plating
Definition: Electroplating with gold to provide high conductivity, corrosion resistance, and decorative appearance.

Label: Nickel Plating
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Coating > Chemical Coating > Plating > Electroplating > Nickel Plating
Definition: Applying a nickel coating by electroplating to improve hardness, corrosion resistance, and wear properties.

Label: Silver Plating
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Coating > Chemical Coating > Plating > Electroplating > Silver Plating
Definition: Electroplating with silver to enhance conductivity, solderability, and decorative qualities.

Label: Tin Plating
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Coating > Chemical Coating > Plating > Electroplating > Tin Plating
Definition: Applying a thin layer of tin to a surface to improve solderability, corrosion resistance, and electrical properties.

Label: Zinc Plating
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Coating > Chemical Coating > Plating > Electroplating > Zinc Plating
Definition: Electroplating steel or iron with zinc to provide sacrificial corrosion protection.

Label: Cladding
Definition: Bonding a layer of one material to the surface of another for improved corrosion resistance or wear properties.

Label: Electrocoating
Definition: A process where electrically charged paint particles are deposited onto a surface for uniform coating and corrosion protection.

Label: Electrodeposited Coating
Definition: A coating formed by electrodeposition, often used for metallic or paint films requiring uniform coverage.

Label: Galvanizing
Definition: The process of applying a protective zinc coating to steel or iron, usually by hot-dip or electroplating, to prevent rust.

Label: Mechanical Coating
Definition: A coating applied mechanically, such as by peening or tumbling, to adhere protective particles onto a metal surface.

Label: Powder Coating
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Coating > Mechanical Coating > Powder Coating
Definition: A dry finishing process where powdered paint is electrostatically applied and cured under heat to form a protective layer.

Label: Metal Coating
Definition: A general term for applying a metallic layer to improve protection, conductivity, or decorative qualities.

Label: Passivation
Definition: A chemical treatment, usually for stainless steel, that removes free iron and enhances the formation of a protective oxide layer.

Label: Phosphate Coating
Definition: A conversion coating that applies a crystalline phosphate layer to steel for corrosion protection and paint adhesion.

Label: Press Forming
Definition: A surface finishing method where materials or coatings are shaped or bonded to a substrate using mechanical pressing.

Label: Painting
Definition: The application of liquid or powder paint to a surface to provide protection and decorative finish.

Label: Wet Painting
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Coating > Painting > Wet Painting
Definition: A conventional painting process where liquid paint is sprayed, brushed, or dipped onto a surface.

Label: Roll Coating
Definition: A coating process where liquid material is applied to a flat substrate using rotating rollers.

Label: Surface Coating
Definition: A general term for applying protective or decorative layers on a material surface, such as paint, plating, or films.

Label: Thermal Coating
Definition: A group of coating processes where materials are deposited on a surface using high-temperature energy sources.

Label: Thermal Spray Coating
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Coating > Thermal Coating > Thermal Spray Coating
Definition: A process where molten or semi-molten material is sprayed onto a surface to form a protective or functional coating.

Label: Flame Spraying
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Coating > Thermal Coating > Thermal Spray Coating > Flame Spraying
Definition: A thermal spray method where coating material is melted by a flame and propelled onto a substrate.

Label: Thermal Spraying
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Coating > Thermal Coating > Thermal Spray Coating > Flame Spraying > Thermal Spraying
Definition: A family of coating processes in which materials are heated and sprayed at high velocity to build surface layers.

Label: Plasma Spraying
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Coating > Thermal Coating > Thermal Spray Coating > Plasma Spraying
Definition: A thermal spray process using a plasma jet to melt and accelerate coating particles onto a surface.

Label: Vaporized Metal Coating
Also Called: Physical Vapor Deposition, Vacuum Metalizing, Vapor Metalizing
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Coating > Thermal Coating > Vaporized Metal Coating
Definition: A process where metals are vaporized in a vacuum and deposited onto a substrate for decorative or functional films.

Label: Chemical Vapor Deposition
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Coating > Thermal Coating > Vaporized Metal Coating > Chemical Vapor Deposition
Definition: A process where volatile chemical precursors react or decompose on a substrate to form a solid thin film.

Label: Plasma Enhanced Chemical Vapor Deposition
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Coating > Thermal Coating > Vaporized Metal Coating > Chemical Vapor Deposition > Plasma Enhanced Chemical Vapor Deposition
Definition: A CVD variation that uses plasma to enhance chemical reactions, enabling lower temperature thin-film deposition.

Label: Physical Vapor Deposition
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Coating > Thermal Coating > Vaporized Metal Coating > Physical Vapor Deposition
Definition: A process where materials are physically vaporized in a vacuum and condensed on a substrate as a thin film.

Label: Vapor Deposition
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Coating > Thermal Coating > Vaporized Metal Coating > Vapor Deposition
Definition: A general term for processes that deposit thin solid films from vapor-phase precursors.

Label: MicroFinishing
Definition: A precision finishing process that removes very small amounts of material to achieve high surface quality and accuracy.

Label: Surface Preparation
Definition: Processes used to clean and condition a surface before finishing, coating, or bonding.

Label: Abrasive Cleaning
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Surface Preparation > Abrasive Cleaning
Definition: Surface cleaning using abrasive particles to remove contaminants, rust, or coatings.

Label: Bead Blasting
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Surface Preparation > Abrasive Cleaning > Bead Blasting
Definition: A blasting process that uses glass or ceramic beads to clean or finish surfaces without significant material removal.

Label: Chemical Cleaning
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Surface Preparation > Abrasive Cleaning > Chemical Cleaning
Definition: Cleaning a surface with chemical solutions to remove oxides, oils, or contaminants.

Label: Surface Blasting
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Surface Preparation > Abrasive Cleaning > Surface Blasting
Definition: A cleaning or finishing process that uses high-speed abrasive particles to remove material or contaminants from surfaces.

Label: Tumbling
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Surface Preparation > Abrasive Cleaning > Tumbling
Definition: A finishing process where parts are placed in a rotating drum with abrasives to deburr, clean, or polish.

Label: Barrel Finishing
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Surface Preparation > Abrasive Cleaning > Tumbling > Barrel Finishing
Definition: A type of tumbling where parts are processed in a rotating barrel with media for surface improvement.

Label: Vibratory Tumbling
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Surface Preparation > Abrasive Cleaning > Tumbling > Vibratory Tumbling
Definition: A tumbling method where parts are placed in a vibrating container with abrasive media for deburring and polishing.

Label: Belt Sanding
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Surface Preparation > Belt Sanding
Definition: A process that uses a continuous abrasive belt to smooth or remove material from surfaces.

Label: Harperizing
Definition: A mass finishing process using rotating tubs or vibratory machines with abrasive media to deburr or polish parts.

Label: Polishing
Definition: A finishing process that smooths a surface using abrasives to achieve a reflective or glossy appearance.

Label: Chemical Polishing
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Surface Preparation > Polishing > Chemical Polishing
Definition: A polishing method that uses controlled chemical reactions to smooth and brighten a material surface.

Label: Pickling
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Surface Preparation > Polishing > Chemical Polishing > Pickling
Definition: A chemical treatment using acids to remove oxides, scale, or impurities from metal surfaces.

Label: Electropolishing
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Surface Preparation > Polishing > Electropolishing
Definition: An electrochemical process that removes surface material to improve smoothness, brightness, and corrosion resistance.

Label: Mechanical Polishing
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Surface Preparation > Polishing > Mechanical Polishing
Definition: A polishing process using physical abrasives or tools to refine a material’s surface finish.

Label: Planarization
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Surface Preparation > Polishing > Planarization
Definition: A precision process that levels and smooths surfaces to achieve uniform flatness, often in semiconductor manufacturing.

Label: Chemical Mechanical Polishing
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Surface Preparation > Polishing > Planarization > Chemical Mechanical Polishing
Definition: A hybrid process combining chemical etching and mechanical abrasion to achieve ultra-flat, defect-free surfaces.

Label: Sand Blasting
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Surface Preparation > Sand Blasting
Definition: A process that propels sand or abrasive particles at high velocity to clean or texture surfaces.

Label: Grit Blasting
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Surface Preparation > Sand Blasting > Grit Blasting
Definition: A blasting method using angular abrasive particles (grit) to roughen or clean surfaces.

Label: Shot Peening
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Surface Preparation > Shot Peening
Definition: A surface treatment where small spherical media are blasted at metal parts to improve fatigue resistance by inducing compressive stresses.

Label: Peening
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Surface Preparation > Shot Peening > Peening
Definition: A cold working process where a surface is mechanically hammered or blasted to improve strength and surface properties.

Label: Ultrasonic Cleaning
Hierarchy: Surface Finishing > Surface Preparation > Ultrasonic Cleaning
Definition: A cleaning process that uses high-frequency ultrasonic waves in a liquid bath to remove contaminants from parts.

Label: Tumble Finishing
Definition: A finishing process where parts are rotated in a barrel or vibratory machine with abrasives for deburring or polishing.

Label: Vibratory Finishing
Definition: A mass finishing process where parts and abrasive media are vibrated together to smooth surfaces or remove burrs.

Label: Textile Process
Definition: A broad group of manufacturing methods used to convert fibers, yarns, or fabrics into finished textiles or products.

Label: Crochet
Definition: A textile technique where yarn is interlaced into loops using a hook to create fabric or decorative items.

Label: Dyeing
Definition: A process of applying color to textile fibers, yarns, or fabrics using dyes to achieve uniform or patterned coloration.

Label: Knitting
Definition: A method of creating fabric by interlocking loops of yarn with needles in either weft or warp structures.

Label: Weaving
Definition: A process of interlacing warp and weft yarns at right angles on a loom to form fabric.

Label: Tool Making
Definition: The process of designing and manufacturing tools, molds, dies, and fixtures used in manufacturing operations.

Label: Die Making
Definition: The specialized craft of creating dies, which are tools used to cut, shape, or form material in stamping and forming operations.

Label: Mold Making
Definition: The process of designing and fabricating molds used in casting, injection molding, or forming processes.

Label: Coremaking
Definition: A process of producing sand or ceramic cores used inside molds to shape internal cavities in castings.

Label: Wood Working
Definition: The craft or manufacturing process of cutting, shaping, and assembling wood into products or structures.
